The riskiest assumption is feasibility (axis F score 3.0 from dvf:7), specifically whether analytic moment matching can accurately propagate uncertainty through deep additive structures in sparse variational Gaussian process Kolmogorov-Arnold networks without destabilizing training or exceeding acceptable computational limits.

The riskiest assumption, driven by feasibility score F: 3.0, is that analytic moment matching and sparse variational Gaussian process inference can scale effectively across complex Kolmogorov-Arnold network topologies without severe degradation in approximation accuracy or convergence stability.
If training time scales worse than O(NM^2) with respect to sample size N and inducing points M, violating the quasi-linear complexity expectation, the approach is killed.

The riskiest assumption is that integrating global-local attention blocks into a lightweight decoder architecture will maintain separation quality while drastically lowering computational overhead, constrained by a feasibility score of 2.0.

Given the feasibility score of 2.0 on axis F, the riskiest assumption is that integrating global-local attention blocks into transformer decoder layers will maintain stable training dynamics and convergence without introducing severe gradient interference or custom kernel bottlenecks.

The riskiest assumption, driven by feasibility axis score 2.0, is that integrating global-local attention into every layer of a lightweight decoder architecture can be trained stably without exceeding target hardware latency or memory limits.

The feasibility score is low at 2.0 because integrating custom global-local attention mechanisms into standard decoder-based transformer architectures may cause instability or fail to preserve long-range dependencies during multi-scale feature fusion.

The feasibility axis score is 2.0 out of 5.0 (dvf:13), which indicates that the riskiest assumption is whether predictive uncertainty estimates derived from operator networks can maintain calibration and stable optimization performance when coupled directly with sequential Bayesian optimization loops on out-of-distribution physical domains.

The riskiest assumption, fixed by feasibility axis F (score 2.0), is that lightweight predictive uncertainty quantification from operator networks can maintain sufficient calibration and stability when integrated directly into active Bayesian optimization loops without incurring prohibitive training or inference slowdowns.
